name: Execute Command
description: Runs a program on the machine that runs Omniscope, once or once per record, passes the input records through and outputs each command's exit code, output and errors.
introductoryText:
Runs a command on the machine where the block runs (the Omniscope server, or the block's Docker container if the server runs custom blocks in Docker), as the user that Omniscope runs as. Use it to start a script, copy or move a file, or call a command-line tool as one step of a workflow. The input records, if any, are passed through unchanged.

**How to set it up**: enter a **Command**, such as `python --version`, or choose a **Field with commands** to run one command per record (the field wins when both are set). Commands run without a shell: pipes, redirects and variables are not available, except through **Run through cmd /c** on Windows (`cmd /c copy C:/Myfile.txt D:/Myfile.txt`). Set a **Time limit** so a command that hangs doesn't hold up the workflow.

By default the block stops at the first command that fails (a non-zero exit code, a program that can't be found, or the time limit), and shows the end of its error output. Tick **Carry on after a failed command** to run the rest and record the failure instead.

**Security**: anyone who can edit a project with this block can run any program the Omniscope user can run, and with **Field with commands** whoever controls the data controls the commands. Only use it on servers where the people who edit projects are trusted with that.

options.name: command
options.title: Command
options.description: The program and its arguments, for example python --version. Leave empty to take commands from a field.

options.name: commands_field
options.title: Field with commands
options.description: A field with one command per record. Records with an empty value are skipped. Only use with data you trust.

options.name: ignoreErrors
options.title: Carry on after a failed command
options.description: Untick (the default) to stop with an error at the first command that fails. Tick to run the rest and record the failure in the Commands output.

options.name: auto_cmd
options.title: Run through cmd /c (Windows)
options.description: Puts "cmd /c" in front of each command, so Windows shell commands such as copy and dir work. The command then runs through the Windows shell.

options.name: timeout
options.title: Time limit (seconds)
options.description: Stop a command that runs longer than this. 0 for no limit.

blockOutputs.label: Commands
blockOutputs.tooltip: One record per command run: cmd, code (exit code), stdout, stderr, and error (why it failed, empty when it worked).
